sections.overview: Described in 1991, this cichlid is known from the upper and lower Xingu basin in Brazil, including the Iriri and Curuá drainages.
sections.identification: The original diagnosis emphasizes reflective silver flank spots and a dark vertical mark below the eye; larger fish develop silvery scales on the front of the flanks.
sections.habitat: Records include clear-water, gently sloping marginal habitats with sand, fine gravel or mud, as well as some floodplain lakes.
sections.diet: Species-specific prey records are sparse; the genus name refers to substrate feeding, but this profile does not assume a detailed diet for this species.
sections.behavior: The original paper records it as the first Geophagus species observed brooding on a substrate, rather than using the mouthbrooding pattern documented in many congeners.
sections.reproduction: The 1991 description reports samples from two parts of the Xingu basin that differ slightly in colour and measurements.
sections.ecology: Within this lot, it contrasts with G. brokopondo, a Suriname-basin member of the surinamensis group whose breeding mode remains unconfirmed; G. crassilabris is another geographically separate congener from Panama. The original paper further notes slight colour and measurement differences between its upper- and lower-basin samples.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global Least Concern assessment dated 7 November 2018; that assessment date should accompany the category.
